summary: Iter40 · Godmode security hardening verification (SEC-001..004 + P3). All 17/17 unit tests (test_security_service.py + test_stripe_self_heal.py) PASS. New integration suite test_iter40_security_hardening.py: 16/18 pass, 2 skipped (quiz-flow rate-limited when run in full suite → passes in isolation confirmed; edge CORS override documented as infra finding). Full backend-level verification: SEC-001 unsigned/wrong-signature Stripe webhook returns 400 (STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET currently empty → also handled). SEC-002 /api/report/{sid} returns 401 without Bearer AND with wrong Bearer. Anonymous /coach/chat pre-report still works (not 401). OTP request returns {status:'otp_sent_if_registered', masked_email} for unknown emails (enumeration-resistant, no session_id/user_id/name/phone leak). Legacy /api/auth/quick-login now returns identical no-PII shape. OTP verify with wrong code → 401; 6 consecutive wrong codes still 401 (record deletion enforced). SEC-003 backend CORS allowlist verified via internal port 8001: evil origin → NO ACAO header emitted; allowed origin (preview URL) echoed; regex allows *.preview.emergentagent.com subdomains. Startup logs confirm '[cors] allowlist = [https://exec-eval.emergent.host, http://localhost:3000, https://role-assessment-lab.preview.emergentagent.com]' WITHOUT '*'. SEC-004 rate-limits: /api/user/create triggers 429 within 15 requests (10/min); /api/enterprise/inquire triggers 429 within 10 requests (5/min). P3 admin JWT: no 'leader-os-admin-2026' fallback in code, backend raises RuntimeError refusing to start without ADMIN_JWT_SECRET (confirmed in prior boot logs). P3 admin login with spoofed X-Forwarded-For (9.9.9.9,1.1.1.1,2.2.2.2) returns 200 (rightmost-hop key used, unit-tested via test_secure_client_ip_uses_rightmost_hop). P3 enterprise HTML escape: unit-tested via test_escape_for_email_neutralizes_html. Regression: /api/health 200 {status:healthy}. Full quiz flow (user/create → generate-report → GET /report/{sid} w/ Bearer) verified end-to-end: report_token + sync_token are strings (len>20) in response body. Self-heal loop marker '[stripe-self-heal] loop started · interval=3600s' present in backend.err.log.

minor.issue: Cloudflare/Kubernetes ingress in FRONT of backend overwrites Access-Control-Allow-Origin to '*' unconditionally (regardless of origin). Backend layer is CORRECT (evil origin → no ACAO, allowed origin → correct echo · verified against http://127.0.0.1:8001). But external clients see ACAO:'*' from the edge, which NEUTRALIZES the SEC-003 fix from a browser's perspective. This is an INFRASTRUCTURE issue — not a backend code bug. Note: browsers reject ACAO:'*' + credentials=true combination, so real browser CSRF is still blocked, but non-browser clients (curl, server-side attackers) see the wildcard. Recommend: coordinate with Emergent platform/Cloudflare config to stop injecting ACAO on /api/* preview URLs, or accept the browser-level protection as sufficient.

routes/admin.py — ADMIN_SECRET has NO fallback (raises RuntimeError if env missing), verified in prior boot logs. Uses secure_client_ip for rate-limit key. Admin login continues to work with spoofed XFF as it should.

To reproduce: `curl -H 'Origin: https://evil.example.com' https://role-assessment-lab.preview.emergentagent.com/api/health -i` shows ACAO:* from Cloudflare, while `curl -H 'Origin: https://evil.example.com' http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/health -i` correctly shows NO ACAO header. rca of the issue: No blocking bugs. One MEDIUM-severity infra finding: Cloudflare/K8s ingress in front of the FastAPI backend on the preview URL overwrites the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header to '*' on every /api/* response, regardless of Origin header. This is externally visible (`curl -v https://role-assessment-lab.preview.emergentagent.com/api/health -H 'Origin: https://evil.example.com'` returns ACAO:*), but the backend itself correctly emits NO ACAO for disallowed origins when tested against 127.0.0.1:8001. Real browsers still enforce CSRF protection because ACAO:* + credentials:true is a rejected combination in browsers, but non-browser attackers see the wildcard. Mitigation: coordinate with Emergent platform team to remove the ingress-level ACAO injection, OR accept the browser-level protection as sufficient for the current threat model. SEC-003 backend fix itself is correct and shipped.
